sampling_model.units: Independent superpopulation draws with \(q_{ni}\sim\mathcal N(0,I_{p_n})\) and \(p_n/n\to\kappa\).
sampling_model.treatment: Binary treatment \(A_{ni}\in\{0,1\}\) with known propensity one half.
sampling_model.outcome: Binary outcome with \(Y_{ni}\mid(q_{ni},A_{ni})\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}\{\sigma(\gamma q_{ni,1})\}\) in both arms.
sampling_model.overlap: Known propensity is exactly one half.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: On each arm's certified strict-feasibility event, the unique exact same-sample entropy weights balance all \(p_n\) coordinates to the pooled empirical mean. On its complement, uniform within-arm weights provide a harmless total finite-sample default and are not called entropy balancing. Every least-squares leverage object uses the Moore--Penrose pseudoinverse for arbitrary \(Q_n\). Oracle DR uses the known conditional mean, while \(\gamma\) is estimated only for phase inference.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 4 gives \(\sqrt n(\widehat\theta^{ep}-\theta^*)\Rightarrow G\) and \(nR_\lambda(\widehat\theta^{ep})\Rightarrow G^\top HG/2\) in fixed policy dimension.
Nonparametrically estimated-propensity IPW attains the semiparametric efficiency bound for the average treatment effect.
The proportional logistic MLE has coordinate and norm limits governed by three scalar state parameters.
Logistic-MLE existence has a sharp Gaussian proportional phase-transition curve.
A convex Gaussian \(M\)-estimator has a deterministic squared-error limit obtained from a finite scalar saddle problem.
A quadratic approximate-balance constraint avoids infeasibility of high-dimensional exact balancing.
The approximate kinematic formula locates random cone-intersection transitions through statistical dimensions up to a square-root-dimensional window.
Entropy balancing has an exponential-tilt dual whose optimum enforces exact covariate moments.
Entropy balancing is doubly robust and can attain semiparametric efficiency under fixed-dimensional model conditions.
A debiased proportional regression adjustment admits a linear-plus-quadratic limit and feasible conservative inference.
Doubly robust policy scores support regret guarantees for empirical policy learning under observational sampling.

body.tldr: A binary randomized trial can use known-propensity IPW, certified exact entropy-balanced IPW with a uniform off-feasibility default, or oracle DR to learn a KL-regularized logistic assignment rule. Population regret reduces exactly to the selected policy norm, and row-sign symmetrization makes only the unconditional marginal true-IPW objective law independent of \(\gamma\). The pooled-target exact-balance threshold and the finite-sample entropy-balanced quadratic identity are established. A same-sample leave-one-out argument now gives a two-sided small-aspect bracket \(c\kappa\le \|b_{E,n}\|_2^2\le C\kappa\) and verifies the leverage criterion needed for conditional concentration, while retaining the nonzero tilt-to-signal and tilt-to-replica Jacobian responses. It does not give a deterministic equivalent, the coefficient of \(\kappa\), or the fixed-\(\lambda\) regret expansion. The joint nonconcave policy phase system and the existence of certified phase strata remain unresolved; phase inference is therefore only a conditional delta-method result on a branch neighborhood constructed independently.

project_justification.gap: FangRidderXie2026 proves efficient penalized-policy regret only for a fixed finite-dimensional rule class, while proportional logistic theory and high-dimensional balancing theory study separate convex estimators. No published result supplies a deterministic equivalent for exact same-sample entropy tilts jointly with the downstream global logistic-policy optimizer; even the reduced entropy-weighted resolvent contains coherent Jacobian responses absent from independent-weight surrogates.
project_justification.niche: The proportional regime makes own-observation leverage, tilt-policy overlap, and tilt-Jacobian response terms order one; it also creates a sharp feasibility boundary. The present solved diagnostic shows that the exact same-sample entropy quadratic has order \(\kappa\) at small aspect ratio and concentrates under an explicit leverage criterion, but it does not determine its leading constant or the sign of a regret dividend.
project_justification.fill: The established contribution combines the deformed-orthant feasibility threshold with an exact conditional quadratic decomposition and a lower-triangular same-row cavity bound. This yields fixed positive finite upper and lower constants for the small-aspect entropy quadratic diagnostic. A finite deterministic tilt-policy system, global selection for the nonconcave objective, exact regret cells, and unconditional phase inference remain subsequent mathematical tasks.

body.related_work: FangRidderXie2026 supplies the benchmark-lottery motivation, the fixed-dimensional regret law, and the rich-balance HIR comparison, but not the proportional same-sample entropy problem. HiranoImbensRidder2003 supplies the classical score-projection mechanism, while the fixed-dimensional reduction in this core shows that balancing only linear coordinates is a partial projection here. SurCandes2019 treats one proportional logistic likelihood, and ThrampoulidisAbbasiHassibi2018 treats convex Gaussian estimators; neither certifies this coupled entropy problem or its nonconcave global policy optimizer. CandesSur2020 and AmelunxenLotzMcCoyTropp2014 provide separation and conic-geometry tools used for the pooled-target threshold. Hainmueller2012 and ZhaoPercival2017 connect entropy duality and exact balance to fixed-dimensional causal efficiency, while DaiYan2024 studies high-dimensional feasibility. LuYangWang2025 motivates retaining diagonal, off-diagonal, and own-row leverage corrections, but does not cover endogenous exponential tilts. The cavity calculation here therefore uses that work only as motivation: its nonzero signal and replica Jacobian blocks are derived for the present weights. AtheyWager2021 supplies the oracle DR policy-score comparator. AshrafKarlanYin2006 is the motivating commitment-savings application, not a claim that its three-arm data follow the Gaussian binary calibration model.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The augmented residual Jacobian is lower triangular but does not close to a finite deterministic state: the blocks \(U_aJ_a^{-1}\) and \(V_a^{\zeta}J_a^{-1}\) remain endogenous functions of the same Gaussian rows. The order argument controls them sufficiently to prove \(\|b_{E,n}\|_2^2=\Theta_{\mathbb P}(\kappa)\) in a small-aspect iterated regime and to make the existing conditional Chebyshev criterion vanish. It does not prove convergence of either conditional-mean term, does not show that its valid interval contains \(\kappa=1/8\), and does not justify interchanging the proportional and small-\(\kappa\) limits with the fixed-\(\lambda\) nonconcave optimizer. Separately, the row criterion need not be concave, so stationary roots do not certify a global selector. No positive, zero, or negative HIR-dividend cell follows from the quadratic order bracket.
body.honest_scope: The established mathematical scope consists of the radial regret identity, unconditional marginal true-IPW \(\gamma\)-invariance, the pooled-target feasibility threshold, fixed-dimensional score projections, the exact entropy-balanced conditional quadratic identity, its exact Bernoulli fluctuation formula, and a small-aspect same-sample order bracket with vanishing leverage criterion. Exact-balance conclusions remain restricted to \(\mathcal E_{0n}\cap\mathcal E_{1n}\cap\mathcal Q_n\); the uniform complement rule only makes finite-sample objects total. The bracket has unspecified fixed constants and concerns the strong-penalty quadratic diagnostic, not the fixed-\(\lambda\) causal regret limit. The coefficient \(r_E=\kappa/(8\lambda)+o(\kappa)\), a finite joint tilt-policy deterministic equivalent, global uniqueness of the selected norms, radius/collision and dividend cells, and ordering relative to oracle DR are not established. The phase-inference calculation is valid only conditionally on an independently constructed, nonabstaining, derivative-nondegenerate certified branch separated from every boundary; no such nonempty stratum is constructed here. Learned outcome regression, non-Gaussian covariates, heterogeneous treatment effects, multiple arms, and a literal model of the savings outcomes remain outside scope.
